# SH4ZAM-DCE

Based on SH4ZAM by Falco Girgis (https://github.com/gyrovorbis/sh4zam). Copyright (c) 2025, 2026 Falco Girgis and SH4ZAM Contributors, MIT License (`LICENSE`).

A header-only sister include of SH4ZAM for the Dreamcast's SH-4: batch routines SH4ZAM does not have, and reworked versions of some of its routines under a `shz_dce_` name with the same signature. On the SH-4 they use FTRV, FIPR and FSRRA; anywhere else they are plain C on SH4ZAM's software back end. SH4ZAM is used as its own library: put its `include` on the path next to `include/` here, then `#include <sh4zam_dce/shz_dce.h>`. `shz_dce_override.h` (not part of that include) puts SH4ZAM's own names on the reworks, one compile-time switch a group of routines (below). `KERNEL_GUIDE.md` says how a routine is written, tested and costed. Thesis: `doc/THESIS.md` (the mathematics, the method, findings about SH4ZAM, a console's results, suggestions for upstream). Handover: `doc/HANDOVER.md`. For upstream: `doc/upstream/shz_asin_acos.h`, the arcsine and arccosine as one file that needs SH4ZAM only.

Checks, all hidden and one at a time (host tests, SH-4 compile checks, the SH-4 code run instruction by instruction in `tests/sh4run`, a cycle ESTIMATE table): `python tests/run_checks.py` with the repository's Python; `--only <topic>` for one header, `--hw-model off` to run without the third party's bit-exact FIPR / FTRV / FSRRA models (`tests/third_party/sh4_fpu_approx`, its own MIT notice, tests only). `tests/sh4run` stops a run on an unaligned load or store, a register a call must keep, a cache line allocated and not filled: a pass is the "alignment: checked" of every instruction a routine executed.

MEASURED on a console (h2 and c4b, 2026-11-25, one console): 21.15 against the plain form's 43.19 in the cache, 58.09 against 74.07 out of it; kept |

Strides for both arrays, in place allowed, both arrays prefetched 64 bytes ahead (`SHZ_DCE_XMTRX_PREFETCH`). SH4ZAM has the single calls and no array form: off the SH-4 these are the loop of its call | YES against the loop of SH4ZAM's single call on the SH-4: the same FTRV, FSRRA and products | a vector: projection 26 -> 11; point3 / vec3 13 -> 9.5 (7.5 without the prefetches); vec4 15 -> 10.5 (9). The projection MEASURED on a console (h3, 2026-11-25, one console): 14.15 / 45.99 a vector in / out of the cache, against KallistiOS's `mat_transform` 13.38 / 42.86: **demoted**, use `mat_transform` on a hot path, keep this only where the bytes must equal SH4ZAM's. The other three: untimed, not for hot paths |

Cycles E are estimates from a model of the SH7750 pipeline on the compiled code, every memory access a cache hit: for comparing two routines, not a console measurement. Code that must reproduce a result bit for bit takes only the routines that say YES.

**Timed on a console, and the rule.** The owner's rule: where SH4ZAM or KallistiOS already has a call that is faster, use theirs. Of the 37 names this layer adds (all but the 21 wrappers below), two have been timed on a console: `shz_dce_pvr_project` (kept: faster than its plain form, and KallistiOS has nothing that writes PVR vertices) and `shz_dce_xmtrx_project_point3_batch` (demoted: slower than `mat_transform`). Every other added name in the table above is **untimed, not for hot paths**: its cycles are the model's only, until a console page shows a gain over the SH4ZAM or KallistiOS call for the same job. The header comments that carry a console's numbers say "Do not overwrite or replace in a SH4ZAM sync pass without re-measuring on a console".

## SH4ZAM first, and the override switches

Falco Girgis ran this layer's reworks on a console (single calls, cycles cached / uncached; `doc/THESIS.md`, section 7, has his table). The arcsine and arccosine won: 850 times closer to the true angle for the same cycles or fewer; with 5 terms the arctangent ended the jitter of an interpolated rotation. The reordered roots, lengths and safe normalisations did not win. SH4ZAM then took the arcsine, arccosine and arctangent as commit cff97e8 (#92, 2026-11-18), gave `shz_inv_sqrtf` and the safe normalisations the reordered form, made `shz_sqrtf` FSQRT and added `shz_opaquef` (master ff39547, 2026-11-22). So every routine this layer had reworked is now SH4ZAM's job, and the layer keeps one implementation of each: SH4ZAM's.

**One implementation where SH4ZAM has one.** Twenty-one `shz_dce_` names call SH4ZAM's routine underneath: the roots, lengths, distances, safe normalisations, the two FIPR names, `shz_dce_asinf`, `shz_dce_acosf`, `shz_dce_atan2f` and `shz_dce_opaquef`. `tests/host/wrap_test.c` holds each to SH4ZAM's bits; `sqrt_test`, `trig_test` and `atan2_test` (and their SH-4 checks) pin what SH4ZAM ff39547 promises for those routines, so a later SH4ZAM change shows up as a named failure ("SH4ZAM ff39547 claim: ..."). The reworked bodies were removed (the last tree with them is 691aa21); a build that sets `SHZ_DCE_REWORK_ROOTS` or `SHZ_DCE_REWORK_FIPR` to 1 stops with an error, and the barrier switches `SHZ_DCE_OPAQUE...` are ignored. This layer needs SH4ZAM master at 3cdff11 or later (`shz_dce_cdefs.h` stops on the 0.10.0 tag, which has neither `SHZ_ATAN2F_TERMS` nor `shz_opaquef`).

`shz_dce_override.h` still defines SH4ZAM's names as macros for the `shz_dce_` names, one switch a group, so code that includes it keeps compiling. Every switch now gives SH4ZAM's own routine by way of the wrapper: the header changes nothing a program computes.

| Switch | Default | SH4ZAM names it renames to the `shz_dce_` wrapper |
|---|---|---|
| `SHZ_DCE_USE_ASIN_ACOS` | 1 | `shz_asinf`, `shz_acosf` |
| `SHZ_DCE_USE_ATAN2` | 1 | `shz_atan2f` |
| `SHZ_DCE_USE_SQRT` | 0 | `shz_sqrtf`, `shz_hypotf` |
| `SHZ_DCE_USE_INV_SQRT` | 0 | `shz_inv_sqrtf` |
| `SHZ_DCE_USE_MAGNITUDE` | 0 | `shz_vec2/3/4_magnitude`, `shz_vec2/3/4_magnitude_inv` |
| `SHZ_DCE_USE_DISTANCE` | 0 | `shz_vec2/3/4_distance` |
| `SHZ_DCE_USE_NORMALIZE` | 0 | `shz_vec2/3/4_normalize_safe` |
| `SHZ_DCE_USE_FIPR` | 0 | `shz_vec4_normalize`, `shz_vec3_magnitude` |
| `SHZ_DCE_OVERRIDE_ALL` | 0 | 1 turns on every switch above that is not set by name |

(The old `SHZ_DCE_OVERRIDE_APPROX` is still read.)

## Acknowledgments

`shz_dce_shadow.h` (`shz_dce_shadow_compare_batch`) is the batch form of the planar shadow-map compare of SH4DER-PVR, Copyright (c) 2026 Jilted Valkyrie (see the LICENSE of that project). The steps are its steps; the code is written here against SH4ZAM's public API and says so in its comments. Credit to SH4DER-PVR and its author is given here, as that project's terms ask.

`shz_dce_shadow.h` and `shz_dce_tri_row.h` are stop-gaps: when SH4ZAM has its own versions of `shz_dce_shadow_compare_batch` and `shz_dce_tri_row_step`, callers move to those and these two headers are removed.
